ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, points $A$, $B$, and $C$ are on circle $\odot O$, with $OB\parallel AC$. Line $BC$ intersects $OA$ at point $D$. If $\angle ADB=60^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle AOB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $ \angle ACB=x^\circ$,\\
then $ \angle AOB=2\angle ACB=2x^\circ$,\\
since $OB\parallel AC$,\\
thus $ \angle OBD=\angle ACB=x^\circ$,\\
since $ \angle ADB=60^\circ$,\\
thus $ \angle AOB+\angle OBD=\angle ADB=60^\circ$, that is $ 2x+x=60$,\\
solving for $x$ gives $ x=20$,\\
then $ \angle AOB=2x^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a circle with O as the center, and the three points A, B, and C are on the circumference; the line segments OA and OB are radii. The straight line BC passes through the inside of the circle and intersects OA at point D, so B, D, and C are collinear, and O, D, and A are collinear. The problem text gives OB ∥ AC, and gives ∠ADB = 60°. Reasoning: Let ∠ACB = x°. Because ∠ACB is an inscribed angle, what it subtends is arc AB, and ∠AOB is the central angle subtending the same arc AB, so ∠AOB = 2x°. method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a circle centered at O with A, B, C on the circumference; OA and OB are radii, D lies on OA where chord/line BC crosses it, and BD is the same line as BC. From the text use OB ∥ AC and ∠ADB = 60°. Let x = ∠ACB. By the inscribed-angle theorem, the central angle ∠AOB subtending arc AB is 2x. Because OB ∥ AC and BD lies on BC, alternate/corresponding angles give ∠OBD = ∠ACB = x. 图像描述：图中是一个以 O 为圆心的圆，A、B、C 三点在圆周上；线段 OA 与 OB 是半径。直线 BC 穿过圆内并与 OA 相交于点 D，因此 B、D、C 共线，且 O、D、A 共线。题目文字给出 OB ∥ AC，并给出 ∠ADB = 60°。

推理：设 ∠ACB = x°。因为 ∠ACB 是圆周角，所对的是弧 AB，而 ∠AOB 是同弧 AB 所对的圆心角，所以 ∠AOB = 2x°。又因为 OB ∥ AC，且 BD 与 BC 是同一直线，所以 ∠OBD = ∠ACB = x°。在三角形 OBD 中，D、O、A 共线，射线 DA 是射线 DO 的延长线，因此 ∠ADB 是三角形 OBD 在 D 点的外角，所以 ∠ADB = ∠AOB + ∠OBD。代入已知 ∠ADB = 60°，得到 2x + x = 60，即 3x = 60，解得 x = 20。因此 ∠AOB = 2x = 40°。

Since $\angle ADB=60^\circ$, $\angle AOB+\angle OBD=\angle ADB=60^\circ$, i.e., $2x+x=60$. Solving gives $x=20$, so $\angle AOB=2x^\circ=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, there is a circle with O as the center, and the three points A, B, and C are on the circumference; the line segments OA and OB are radii. The straight line BC passes through the inside of the circle and intersects OA at point D, so B, D, and C are collinear, and O, D, and A are collinear. The problem text gives OB ∥ AC, and gives ∠ADB = 60°.

Reasoning: Let ∠ACB = x°. Because ∠ACB is an inscribed angle, what it subtends is arc AB, and ∠AOB is the central angle subtending the same arc AB, so ∠AOB = 2x°. Also because OB ∥ AC, and BD and BC are the same straight line, ∠OBD = ∠ACB = x°. In triangle OBD, D, O, and A are collinear, and ray DA is the extension of ray DO, therefore ∠ADB is the exterior angle at point D of triangle OBD, so ∠ADB = ∠AOB + ∠OBD. Substituting the known ∠ADB = 60°, obtain 2x + x = 60, namely 3x = 60, solving gives x = 20. Therefore ∠AOB = 2x = 40°.
